findings.reason: adding a `<link>` or meta tag to `docs/index.html` would silently not appear in the `file:` capture, so the golden-path capture measures a page that has diverged from the served one; extending `write_file_spa_document` to render the shell keeps one owner of the document shape and one stylesheet list.
findings.text: `write_file_spa_document` (tests/spa_browser_harness.py:557) builds a second SPA document skeleton and a second hardcoded stylesheet list (`_SPA_STYLESHEETS`, tests/spa_browser_harness.py:33) instead of rendering the canonical shell `docs/index.html` through `reckon/serve.py::_render_spa_html(relative_assets=True)`, which already reads that shell and rewrites `/`-prefixed asset URLs to relative — the exact requirement of a `file:` load.

findings.reason: naming the renderer turns the node from "write a document composer" into "extend the renderer to inline its assets", a smaller change with the shell as the single source for both the stylesheet and script inventories.
findings.text: §6 proposes the delivery path without citing the existing document renderer it extends, so it reads as net-new machinery when `reckon/serve.py::_render_spa_html(relative_assets=True)` already produces the same shell for the static `build` command, the only difference being inline-vs-copy of the referenced assets.

findings.reason: the asymmetry is a latent drift (the script list tracks the shell, the stylesheet list does not), and deriving stylesheets the same way — or rendering the shell — removes the second inventory.
findings.text: one part of the composition is split shallowly: `_SPA_STYLESHEETS` duplicates the shell's `<link>` inventory while `authored_ui_module_paths` (`:65`) derives the script order from the same shell.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `write_file_spa_document` hides the whole composition (runtime bundles, stylesheet inlining, eleven UI modules compiled through the production compiler, state injection, `</script` escaping) behind one small function, and `file_spa` reuses the existing `ServedSpa` / `_evaluate_browser_url` probe path rather than forking a second harness.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the `file:` path re-implements the SPA document skeleton and its stylesheet inventory rather than rendering the shell owned by `reckon/serve.py` and `docs/index.html`.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §6 names the shared harness and the classifier machinery, but omits the served-document renderer (`reckon/serve.py::_render_spa_html`, `docs/index.html`) that the `file:` path needs, and the landed node then re-derived the shell skeleton instead of extending it.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §6 states the required justification for a parallel layer: the shared harness serves the SPA over `http://127.0.0.1` on an ephemeral port, "the one thing the browser cannot reach", so the served path cannot be extended to cover `file:` and a second delivery path is the honest change.
